speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, and welcome to Grey Matter, the podcast from Greylock.
zh: 大家好，欢迎收听 Greylock 的播客 Grey Matter。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we're featuring another episode of Product-Led AI, the series hosted by Greylock partner Seth Rosenberg, where he discusses opportunities in the application layer of AI.
zh: 今天，我们带来 Product-Led AI 系列的另一期节目，该系列由 Greylock 合伙人 Seth Rosenberg 主持，探讨 AI 应用层的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: His guest this week is Mustafa Suleiman, who leads Microsoft's AI efforts.
zh: 他本周的嘉宾是 Mustafa Suleiman，他领导着 Microsoft 的 AI 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can find more information about this episode and the entire series at productledaipod.com.
zh: 你可以在 productledaipod.com 上找到关于本期节目以及整个系列的更多信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, here's Seth with Product-Led AI.
zh: 现在，有请 Seth 带来 Product-Led AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, I'm Seth Rosenberg.
zh: 大家好，我是 Seth Rosenberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a partner at Greylock and the host of Product-Led AI, a series exploring the opportunities at the application layer of AI.
zh: 我是 Greylock 的合伙人，也是 Product-Led AI 的主持人，这是一个探索 AI 应用层机会的系列节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mustafa, thanks so much for joining.
zh: Mustafa，非常感谢你来参加节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, Seth.
zh: 嘿，Seth。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good to see you again.
zh: 很高兴再次见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: So very excited to have Mustafa here.
zh: 能请到 Mustafa 来我非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: As many people in the audience will know, Mustafa is one of the leading pioneers in AI.
zh: 正如很多听众会知道的那样，Mustafa 是 AI 领域领先的先驱者之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's currently the CEO of AI at Microsoft, venture partner at Greylock.
zh: 他目前是 Microsoft 的 AI CEO，也是 Greylock 的风险合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Former co-founder of Inflection AI, as well as co-founder of DeepMind, which was of course acquired by Google, where he became VP of AI at Google.
zh: 他曾是 Inflection AI 的联合创始人，也是 DeepMind 的联合创始人，DeepMind 后来当然被 Google 收购，他在那里成为了 Google 的 AI 副总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Mustafa, I feel very privileged to be able to work with you through Greylock, but also to have you here to kind of share your take on the current space, which is evolving so quickly.
zh: 所以 Mustafa，能通过 Greylock 与你共事我深感荣幸，同时也很高兴你能来这里分享你对当前这个发展如此迅速的领域的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe to kick it off, I'm curious to hear more about how you decided to focus your career on AI before it was obvious.
zh: 那么作为开场，我很好奇想多了解一下，你是在这件事还不明显的时候，是如何决定把职业生涯聚焦在 AI 上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of strange looking back on it.
zh: 回头看这件事有点奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I sort of had to write my TED talk recently and I reflected on how crazy things are 15 years later.
zh: 我最近不得不写我的 TED 演讲，我回顾了 15 年后的今天事情有多么疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we first started talking about founding DeepMind in 2010, it's hard to overstate how weird we were.
zh: 当我们 2010 年最初开始谈论创立 DeepMind 时，怎么强调我们当时有多怪异都不为过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often people say being an entrepreneur is choosing to obsessively work on something that is really contrarian and attempting something that everybody else thinks is impossible.
zh: 人们常说，做创业者就是选择痴迷地做一件真正反常规的事情，尝试一件其他所有人都认为不可能的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in our case, people didn't just think it was impossible.
zh: 我想在我们的情况里，人们不只是认为它不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: They thought it was completely absurd.
zh: 他们认为它完全是荒谬的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I honestly am not quite sure how we came to have so much faith in our ability to try to do something so out of distribution and exceptional.
zh: 说实话，我不太确定我们当时是怎么对自己有如此大的信心，去尝试做一件如此超出分布、如此非凡的事情的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the initial insight around DeepMind?
zh: 关于 DeepMind 最初的洞察是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we didn't just start working on...
zh: 我的意思是，我们不只是开始做……

speaker: Unknown
en: AI or machine learning.
zh: AI 或者机器学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were fully committed to working on artificial general intelligence, producing a system that could exceed human capabilities and knowledge at all levels.
zh: 我们全身心投入到人工通用智能的研究上，要造出一个能在所有层面超越人类能力和知识的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason we were motivated to do that is because we genuinely wanted to use AI to solve other problems and to make the world a better place.
zh: 而我们之所以有动力这样做，是因为我们真心想用 AI 去解决其他问题，让世界变得更美好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there was no academic lab or setting that could accommodate the scale of investment that we thought was necessary at that time.
zh: 我认为当时没有任何学术实验室或环境能够容纳我们认为必要的投资规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: In academic labs, there wasn't a focus on large-scale engineering.
zh: 在学术实验室里，并没有对大规模工程的关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: There certainly wasn't a focus on products.
zh: 肯定也没有对产品的关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even in the kind of big national project investments that you get from like working in a government, there was just nothing that was like a technical effort to try to understand what intelligence was at scale and deploy it at important problems.
zh: 甚至在那些像在政府工作那样能获得的大型国家项目投资中，也完全没有任何像样的技术性努力，去尝试大规模地理解智能是什么，并将其部署到重要问题上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was really only like
zh: 所以实际上只有

speaker: Unknown
en: Startups that were as brave and courageous, I think, as was necessary to be successful on this mission.
zh: 创业公司才具备完成这项使命所必需的那种勇敢和胆识。

speaker: Unknown
en: By that point, that was my third effort at a company, and it just felt like this is the only vehicle.
zh: 到那时为止，那已经是我第三次创办公司的尝试了，我感觉这是唯一的载体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you learn so much along the way by screwing it up and figuring out how to do it right.
zh: 因为在这一路上，你会通过搞砸和摸索出正确做法学到非常多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had come off the back of a bunch of years working in the nonprofit sector, in governments, in conflict resolution of facilitation.
zh: 在那之前，我曾在非营利部门、政府、冲突调解与斡旋领域工作了多年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd started two small companies, actually one that was focused on selling networking equipment and electronic point of sale systems to restaurants.
zh: 我创办过两家小公司，实际上其中一家专注于向餐厅销售网络设备和电子销售点系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this was like way before that was possible.
zh: 但那是在那种事情变得可能之前的很久。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a failure.
zh: 那是一次失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing I sort of realized is that we need more knowledge and insight in our world to help us address the overwhelming complexity of our systems.
zh: 而我大致意识到的是，我们的世界需要更多的知识和洞见，来帮助我们应对系统那压倒性的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so difficult to make an intervention into a complex social system today, like an economy or a food production system or the financial system, and be confident that that intervention is going to make the impact that you think it is.
zh: 今天，要介入一个复杂的社会系统——比如一个经济体、一个食品生产系统或金融系统——并且确信这个介入会产生你认为会产生的影响，这是极其困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really, I think, one of the reasons why we need amazing AIs.
zh: 而我认为，这正是我们需要出色的 AI 的原因之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to be able to make good predictions about complexity in our world in order to create value and to change that world to help people live healthier and better lives.
zh: 我们需要能够对我们世界中的复杂性做出好的预测，从而创造价值、改变这个世界，帮助人们过上更健康、更美好的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds super cheesy, but that is really what was motivating us back then and still does.
zh: 这听起来超级俗套，但这确实就是当时激励着我们的东西，现在依然是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious.
zh: 我很好奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you had this mission that unlocking abundant intelligence for the world would actually solve problems that matter.
zh: 所以你有这样一个使命：为世界解锁充裕的智能，这将真正解决重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you actually define intelligence in this context?
zh: 在这个语境下，你究竟是如何定义智能的？

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that gave me confidence that we might actually be able to make progress towards inventing intelligence was our third co-founder, Shane Legge, had spent his entire PhD researching
zh: 让我有信心相信我们真的可能朝着发明智能取得进展的一点，是我们的第三位联合创始人 Shane Legge，他用了整个博士生涯研究

speaker: Unknown
en: various definitions of intelligence and trying to aggregate them into a single metric that we could use to turn the science of intelligence and the neuroscience of understanding biological intelligence into
zh: 关于智能的各种定义，并尝试把它们聚合成一个单一的指标，我们可以用它把智能科学和理解生物智能的神经科学变成

speaker: Unknown
en: An engineering effort and really make that a measurable kind of quantifiable exercise.
zh: 一项工程努力，真正使其成为一种可测量的、可量化的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the definition that he came up with was the ability to perform well across a wide range of environments.
zh: 他提出的定义是：在广泛范围的环境中表现良好的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, emphasizing generality.
zh: 所以，这再次强调了通用性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was like a major...
zh: 这就像是一个重大……

speaker: Unknown
en: Now everyone takes the AGI part for granted as though G is the central part of intelligence, but that's an assumption.
zh: 现在每个人都把 AGI 中的这个部分视为理所当然，仿佛 G 是智能的核心，但那只是一个假设。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, generality happens to be one of the characteristics of intelligence, but it's not the only important characteristic.
zh: 你知道，通用性恰好是智能的特征之一，但它并不是唯一重要的特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it also turns out there's also very hard to measure and to scale it down to something that you can really grasp.
zh: 而且事实证明，它也非常难以测量，难以缩减到某种你真正能把握的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas
zh: 而

speaker: Unknown
en: Another sort of definition was the Turing test, of course, is that a system would be intelligent if it could deceive a human into thinking that it was itself a human during natural conversation.
zh: 另一种定义是图灵测试，当然，如果一个系统能够在自然对话中欺骗人类，让人类以为它自己是人类，那它就是智能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in some ways we've sort of crossed the threshold of that intelligence, right?
zh: 而在某些方面，我们某种程度上已经跨越了那个智能的门槛，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have systems now that are really very good at conversation and at least for a few turns could, you know, it's certainly better than humans in many respects, right?
zh: 我们现在拥有的系统非常擅长对话，至少在几个回合内可以，你知道，它在许多方面肯定比人类更好，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can still tell that it's an AI or a chatbot and not a human, but in a few years' time, you really won't be able to tell.
zh: 你仍然能分辨出它是一个 AI 或聊天机器人而不是人类，但再过几年，你真的将无法分辨。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet that doesn't really tell us anything about whether these systems are actually intelligent.
zh: 然而这并不能真正告诉我们这些系统是否真的具有智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, every time we cross a threshold in terms of a benchmark or a milestone in AI, you then sort of turn around and go, okay, well, here are all the problems with that mechanism of measurement.
zh: 你知道，每当我们跨越人工智能基准或里程碑上的一个门槛时，你就会回过头来说，好吧，这种测量机制有这些那些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's the next sort of thing that we need to measure.
zh: 而这是我们接下来需要测量的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard Reed say that AGI is the AI that we don't yet have.
zh: 我听过 Reed 说，AGI 就是我们还没有的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of always pushed forward in the future.
zh: 它总是被推向未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like the constant carrot that we dangle to chase ahead, you know, to sort of move ahead.
zh: 它就像我们挂在前面引诱自己去追逐、去前进的那根永恒的胡萝卜，你知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So another measure that I had proposed is that we should focus more on the capabilities of the system, the actions, the things that it can do, the things that we can observe, that it can have an impact in some environment, rather than this kind of abstract idea of
zh: 所以我提出的另一个衡量标准是，我们应该更多关注系统的能力，即行动、它能做的事情、我们能观察到的、它能在某种环境中产生影响的东西，而不是这种抽象的概念：

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it general or is it good at having conversation?
zh: 它是不是通用的？或者它是不是擅长对话？

speaker: Unknown
en: That would basically be like, can it produce human quality labor in a practical environment and actually earn money for that?
zh: 那基本上就是：它能否在实际环境中产出人类质量的劳动并真正为此赚到钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or could it write software, for example?
zh: 或者比如说，它能编写软件吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very measurable thing.
zh: 这是非常可测量的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I sort of called that a modern Turing test and said that in the next five years, a system would be able to take a very abstract goal, like go create a new product.
zh: 我某种程度上称之为现代图灵测试，并说在未来五年内，一个系统将能够接受一个非常抽象的目标，比如去创造一个新产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get that sort of designed, manufactured, drop shipped, and then distributed and marketed and try and earn a profit from it.
zh: 让它被设计、制造、代发货，然后分销、营销，并尝试从中赚取利润。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you could measure that profit in terms of making a million dollars or something like that.
zh: 然后你就可以用赚一百万美元之类的标准来衡量那个利润。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's going to be a system that could actually do that certainly before 2030.
zh: 我认为在 2030 年之前，肯定会有一系统能真正做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's amazing.
zh: 是的，那太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's possible, do you expect that that type of system would actually trade off on the G, on the generalizability, and it's actually built for a specific use case?
zh: 还有一种可能，你是否预期那类系统实际上会在 G 上做权衡，也就是通用性，而它实际上是为特定用例构建的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that it's more likely that we'll have really powerful systems that are specialized for specific use cases that have real deep domain expertise than we're going to have this sort of very general purpose system that can switch from being a marketer to a clinician, to being a doctor, to being a lawyer, whatever.
zh: 是的，我认为更有可能的是，我们将拥有针对特定用例专门化、拥有真正深厚领域专业知识的真正强大的系统，而不是那种可以从营销人员切换到临床医生、再到医生、再到律师等等的非常通用的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, clearly the general case is going to come afterwards.
zh: 我是说，显然通用的情况会在那之后到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to spend a moment just getting your take of just the state of large models today.
zh: 所以我想花一点时间，听听你对当今大型模型现状的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe you wanted to start with just level setting for the audience of what was the inflection point that led us to the current state of the GPT-3, GPT-4 style models, the inflection 2.5 style models, this combination of the transformer architecture and scaled compute?
zh: 也许你想先给听众做个基础铺垫，是什么拐点把我们带到了 GPT-3、GPT-4 风格模型、inflection 2.5 风格模型的当前状态，也就是 transformer 架构和规模化算力的结合？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that this revolution has been driven by deep learning.
zh: 我认为这场革命是由深度学习驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are still building deep learning models, albeit with a slightly different flavour now, the Transformer architecture from 2017.
zh: 我们仍然在构建深度学习模型，尽管现在口味稍有不同，即 2017 年的 Transformer 架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're now turning those into composable units that are essentially going to act like parts of our software development ecosystem.
zh: 而我们现在正在把它们变成可组合的单元，它们基本上将像我们软件开发生态系统的组成部分一样运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just going to turn to your AI and it's going to actually generate code for you.
zh: 你只需要转向你的 AI，它就会真正为你生成代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we're already sort of seeing that GAP Copilot and, you know, we're seeing it like as a member of your team, able to take a natural language instruction.
zh: 我是说，我们已经某种程度上看到了，GAP Copilot，你知道，我们看到它就像你团队的一员，能够接受自然语言指令。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just act in unison with you.
zh: 并与你协同行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that what people sort of don't quite realize is that these models are not going to be large forever.
zh: 而且我认为人们某种程度上没有完全意识到的是，这些模型不会永远庞大下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the history of all technologies that have been valuable, anything that is significant gets cheaper and easier to use over time.
zh: 在所有有价值技术的历史中，任何重要的事物都会随着时间变得更便宜、更易用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that curve is sort of double exponential over the last like couple of years.
zh: 而在过去像几年里，那条曲线某种程度上是双指数的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible.
zh: 这令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Microsoft AI just released PHYS 3, fully open source.
zh: 我是说，Microsoft AI 刚刚发布了 PHYS 3，完全开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is close to, but not quite at GPT-4 level.
zh: 它接近但尚未完全达到 GPT-4 水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fully open source.
zh: 它是完全开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 3.8 billion parameters.
zh: 它有 38 亿个参数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's like more than a hundred X smaller in terms of inference compute than basically the absolute frontier of models today.
zh: 所以在推理计算方面，这基本上比当今最前沿的模型小了一百多倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I said, it's not quite as good, but it's certainly, you know, as good as or better than GPT 3.5.
zh: 就像我说的，它没那么好，但它肯定，你知道的，和 GPT 3.5 一样好或者更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's mind blowing.
zh: 这太令人震惊了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's something that can fit on your laptop or on a phone, like, I mean, the future.
zh: 我是说，这是可以装进你的笔记本或手机里的东西，就像，我是说，这就是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so.
zh: 所以呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should expect that trajectory to continue.
zh: 我们应该期待这个轨迹继续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think open source models are going to be very close behind the closed source proprietary API models months or maybe even just a year or a year and a half or something.
zh: 我认为开源模型会紧紧跟随闭源专有 API 模型，落后几个月，或者甚至只是一年或一年半之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just going to change the whole creation landscape basically.
zh: 而这基本上会改变整个创作格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: What enabled this model to be kind of almost equal in performance while also being much smaller?
zh: 是什么让这个模型在性能几乎持平的同时还小得多？

speaker: Unknown
en: For the last couple of years, everybody has been focused on reinforcement learning from human feedback.
zh: 在过去几年里，每个人都专注于基于人类反馈的强化学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where in the final stages of training, at the stage of fine tuning or post training, as people say, you have a bunch of trained raters or judges that compare two possible responses or completions from a model.
zh: 在训练的最后阶段，也就是微调阶段或者说人们所说的后训练阶段，你有一批受过训练的评分员或裁判，他们会比较一个模型给出的两个可能的回答或补全。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that pairwise comparison provides large scale feedback for the kinds of behaviors that you want your model to exhibit.
zh: 这种成对比较为你希望模型展现的行为类型提供了大规模的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's familiar with that now.
zh: 现在每个人都很熟悉这个了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we've been focused on as soon as that was showing promising signs, so for the last 18, 24 months, is reinforcement learning from AI feedback, where we really want very smart and capable models to do that pairwise comparison, because obviously we can automate that process and we can produce an even larger number of supervised
